intro: Place value is the idea that a digit's worth depends on where it sits: the 4 in 40 means four tens, not four. This branch shows how tens and hundreds are built from ones, which makes bigger numbers and later arithmetic make sense.

I.3.01.what: Understanding that ten single things can be grouped together and thought of as one ten.

levels.a: Works out how many more sticks are needed to make a bundle of 10.
levels.b: Works out how many more counters fill a box of ten spaces (a ten-frame).
levels.c: Recognizes a group of 10 as "one ten."
levels.d: Knows how many ones make a given number of tens, such as 2 tens being 20 ones.

I.3.02.what: Seeing that each teen number is one ten plus some extra ones, like 16 being ten and six.

levels.a: Says how many tens and ones make 11 to 15, using blocks (a rod is ten, a small cube is one).
levels.c: Picks the blocks that show a given teen number.
levels.d: Reads the teen number shown by a set of blocks.

I.3.03.what: Breaking numbers up to 50 into tens and ones.

levels.a: Knows the names for groups of tens: ten, twenty, thirty and so on.
levels.b: Finds a total by counting the tens first, then counting on the ones.
levels.c: Says how many tens and ones are needed to build a number.
levels.d: Reads the number shown by a set of tens and ones blocks.

I.3.04.what: Understanding two-digit numbers up to 99: the left digit counts tens and the right digit counts ones.

levels.a: Says whether a digit stands for tens or ones.
levels.b: Gives what a digit is worth, such as the 8 in 28 being worth 8.
levels.c: Builds a number from tens and ones, such as 3 tens and 1 one making 31.
levels.d: Tells apart numbers with swapped digits, like 28 and 82.

I.3.05.what: Swapping between ones and tens: ten ones can become a ten, and a ten can be broken back into ones.

levels.a: Bundles 10 loose ones into a ten and says the new count of tens and ones.
levels.b: Breaks a ten into 10 ones and says the new count.
levels.c: Recognizes a number shown two ways, like 27 as 1 ten and 17 ones.
levels.d: Works out a missing number of tens in such an unusual arrangement.
levels.e: Spots the one arrangement of tens and ones that does not make the given number.
levels.f: Finds every different way to show a number with tens and ones blocks.

I.3.06.what: Understanding that ten tens make a hundred, and building numbers in the hundreds.

levels.a: Works out how many more tens are needed to make 100.
levels.c: Says how many hundreds, tens and ones make a three-digit number.
levels.d: Reads the three-digit number shown by a set of blocks.

I.3.07.what: Knowing what each digit in a three-digit number stands for: hundreds, tens or ones.

levels.a: Finds the hundreds digit, which is the one on the left.
levels.b: Finds the tens digit (middle) and the ones digit (right).
levels.c: Says what a digit is worth, such as the 8 in 819 being worth 800.
levels.d: Understands a zero digit means none of that place, as in 208.
levels.e: Builds a number from hundreds, tens and ones given in a mixed-up order.
levels.f: Arranges three digit cards to make the biggest number, sometimes one that must be even.

I.3.08.what: Writing a number as the sum of what each digit is worth, like 47 as 40 + 7 (expanded form).

levels.a: Writes a two-digit number as tens plus ones, like 28 = 20 + 8.
levels.b: Writes a three-digit number as hundreds plus tens plus ones.
levels.c: Turns a split-up number back into an ordinary one, like 200 + 80 + 8 = 288.
levels.d: Handles numbers with a zero in them, like 280 or 305.

I.3.09.what: Reading and writing numbers as words, such as thirty-two or two hundred eighty-five.

levels.a: Matches number words to numbers up to 100.
levels.b: Writes numbers up to 20 as words.
levels.c: Writes numbers up to 100 as words.
levels.d: Reads and writes numbers up to 1,000 as words.

I.3.10.what: Finding the number that is 10 more or 10 less, and later 100 more or less, than a given number.

levels.a: Finds 10 more or less by moving down or up a row on a chart of 1 to 100.
levels.b: Finds 10 more or less mentally by changing the tens digit.
levels.c: Finds 100 more or less by changing the hundreds digit.
levels.d: Finds 10 more or less when it crosses a hundred, like 108 down to 98.

I.3.11.what: Getting to know the hundred chart, a grid of the numbers 1 to 100 arranged in rows of ten.

levels.a: Finds a given number's spot on the chart.
levels.b: Knows that numbers go up by 1 along a row and by 10 down a column.
levels.c: Fills in missing numbers on the chart.
levels.d: Spots patterns, such as which numbers share a row.

I.3.12.what: Comparing numbers by looking at the biggest place first, such as the hundreds or tens.

levels.a: Compares two-digit numbers by their tens.
levels.b: Knows a three-digit number is bigger than any two-digit number.
levels.c: Compares numbers with the same first digit by looking at the next digit.
levels.d: Puts a list of numbers in order from least to greatest.
levels.e: Chooses the missing digit that makes a comparison true, such as 'blank 8 is more than 59'.
levels.f: Works out how many different digits could fill the gap and keep a comparison true.
